questions: What is the brand mission, intention and point of view?
Who are its audiences and what contexts/access needs matter?
What should people recognize, feel or understand?
Which channels, languages and assets are in scope?

logoSystems.title: Logo systems
questions: Which primary mark, wordmark, symbol, secondary, monochrome and small-size variants exist?
Where may each appear, at what minimum size and with what clear space?
What proportions, placement, backgrounds and alterations are prohibited?
Which files are owned, licensed or pending, and what is the fallback if a mark is unavailable?
logoSystems.designA11yReference: Original wordmark retained; clean brand symbol 40:15; notched favicon 11:16. Asset-specific clear-space/minimum-size review remains required.
logoSystems.definitionStatus: Use explicit approved, proposed, pending or not-applicable status per decision.

brandPalette.title: Brand color palette
questions: What are the primary, secondary and accent signature colors?
What emotional, cultural or symbolic associations are intended, and in which contexts?
Which combinations, proportions and backgrounds express the brand?
How do brand colors map separately to UI text, surface, action, error, warning, success and focus roles?
brandPalette.designA11yReference: Aubergine, Petal, Blush, Rose and Copper remain the reference anchors. Do not infer universal emotional effects or substitute accents for validated status colors.
brandPalette.definitionStatus: Use explicit approved, proposed, pending or not-applicable status per decision.

brandTypography.title: Brand typography and display
questions: Which display and supporting families express the identity?
What hierarchy, weight, tracking, case and typesetting give it personality?
What reading/UI fonts, language coverage and fallbacks are required?
What licenses apply, and where must specialty display type be restricted?
brandTypography.designA11yReference: Anton display and Archivo reusable body/UI; live-site Proxima Nova mapping is separate. Original vector wordmark is not regenerated by changing a font.
brandTypography.definitionStatus: Use explicit approved, proposed, pending or not-applicable status per decision.

graphicLanguage.title: Graphic language and motifs
questions: What signature shapes, patterns, dividers, frames or composition devices create recognition?
What meaning, hierarchy and frequency should they carry?
How do they adapt across web, social, print and motion?
What should be absent or restrained, and where are quiet reading zones?
graphicLanguage.designA11yReference: Frame, seam and Surface Field have distinct roles. They are DesignA11y expressions; downstream brands may replace or omit them.
graphicLanguage.definitionStatus: Use explicit approved, proposed, pending or not-applicable status per decision.

iconographyIllustration.title: Iconography and illustration
questions: Does the brand need a proprietary illustration world, functional icons, or both?
What stroke, corner, fill, perspective, detail and optical scale rules apply?
What subjects, metaphors and representational choices fit the brand?
Which rights-cleared asset sources and accessibility naming rules apply?
iconographyIllustration.designA11yReference: Original functional UI icon drafts exist. A full brand illustration world is not yet defined; do not pretend generic UI icons establish that direction.
iconographyIllustration.definitionStatus: Use explicit approved, proposed, pending or not-applicable status per decision.

photographyArtDirection.title: Photography and art direction
questions: What subjects, settings, casting and representation support the brand mission?
What lighting, composition, lens/perspective, color grading and retouching rules apply?
What image and background references are useful, and exactly what should be learned from each?
Are tactile/sensory surfaces appropriate for this brand; which texture, finish, density, intensity and exclusions fit?
outputs: image purpose, crop and text-safe zones
sensory surface brief and quality rubric
photographyArtDirection.designA11yReference: Continuous tactile fields are established; smooth/rough/spiky and glossy/matte/velvet/sanded variety is allowed. Isolated abstract objects are excluded for the surface layer. A photography/casting direction remains to be defined or intentionally marked not applicable.
photographyArtDirection.definitionStatus: Use explicit approved, proposed, pending or not-applicable status per decision.

voiceTone.title: Voice and tone
questions: What personality, point of view and communication principles should people recognize?
How should tone change across editorial, marketing, help, errors and social?
What vocabulary, spelling, terminology, naming and phrases are preferred or prohibited?
How should the brand discuss disability, AI, uncertainty and accessibility claims?
voiceTone.designA11yReference: Inclusive design, accessibility, lived experience and AI define the content context. Formal vocabulary and channel-tone matrices need an explicit brand-owner decision; generic designer samples must not replace the context.
voiceTone.definitionStatus: Use explicit approved, proposed, pending or not-applicable status per decision.

brandMotion.title: Brand motion and animation
questions: What pacing, rhythm, easing and kinetic personality express the identity?
Which signature transitions or graphic movements belong to brand storytelling?
How do video/social motion and functional interface feedback differ?
What static/reduced-motion alternatives, interruption, flashing and intensity constraints apply?
brandMotion.designA11yReference: Frame, seam and field expression plus finite interaction recipes are documented. Brand storytelling does not authorize autoplay or continuous UI motion; focus remains static.

agentRules: Ask about every category; do not infer that missing answers mean approval.
Allow not applicable with a reason and a safe fallback; do not force photography or sensory materials onto every brand.
For references ask what to borrow conceptually and what to reject; reference access is not redistribution permission.
Separate brand expression from functional UI semantics and accessibility behavior.
Create a reviewable profile with field-level source, decision owner, status and rationale before applying it to a copy.
Apply approved choices centrally through theme variables/styles/asset slots; keep stable component APIs.
Revalidate accessibility after adaptation; inherited rules do not certify the outcome.
Keep private reference materials and source permissions out of distributable copies.

questions: Which applications matter: website/app, packaging, print, social posts/stories, video, email, signage, events or other environments?
Should marks or symbol geometry generate repeat patterns, frames, dividers or other motifs? Which transformations preserve recognition?
What pattern density, rhythm, scale, spacing, orientation, crop, contrast and quiet zones fit each context?
Which signature backgrounds are graphic motifs, tactile surfaces, photography or illustration, and what purpose does each serve?
What message hierarchy, information density, aspect ratios and production constraints apply to each channel?
Which expressions remain recognizable without the logo, and which require the primary mark?
What should vary by campaign or asset, and what must stay stable?
Are print production, captions/transcripts, alt text, safe zones or accessible digital equivalents required?
outputs: shared motif grammar and prohibited transformations
format, crop, density and quiet-zone rules
examples of consistent variation, not identical scaled layouts
principles: Derive original motifs from the brand's own assets and purpose; never copy reference designers' artwork.
Repeated marks are graphic brand expression, distinct from continuous tactile sensory surfaces.
Do not force a sensory visual style, mascot, photography or packaging onto a brand that does not need it.
Social/video/packaging inherit the identity and accessible-communication rules; interactive UI mechanics apply only where interaction exists.

surfaceField.rule: Resolve the informal alias to the existing Surface Field element; do not create a duplicate. Sensory describes purpose, not a separate element name.
